func TestDeleteMemoStore(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	ctx := context.Background()
	ts := NewTestingStore(ctx, t)
	user, err := createTestingHostUser(ctx, ts)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	memoCreate := &store.Memo{
		UID:        "test-resource-name",
		CreatorID:  user.ID,
		Content:    "test_content",
		Visibility: store.Public,
	}
	memo, err := ts.CreateMemo(ctx, memoCreate)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, memoCreate.Content, memo.Content)
	err = ts.DeleteMemo(ctx, &store.DeleteMemo{
		ID: memo.ID,
	})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	ts.Close()
}

func TestMemoGetByID(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	ctx := context.Background()
	ts := NewTestingStore(ctx, t)
	user, err := createTestingHostUser(ctx, ts)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	memo, err := ts.CreateMemo(ctx, &store.Memo{
		UID:        "test-memo-1",
		CreatorID:  user.ID,
		Content:    "test content",
		Visibility: store.Public,
	})
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Get by ID
	found, err := ts.GetMemo(ctx, &store.FindMemo{ID: &memo.ID})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, found)
	require.Equal(t, memo.ID, found.ID)
	require.Equal(t, memo.Content, found.Content)

	// Get non-existent

	notFound, err := ts.GetMemo(ctx, &store.FindMemo{ID: &nonExistentID})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Nil(t, notFound)

	ts.Close()
}

SQLite has foreign keys disabled in its DSN, so ON DELETE CASCADE for memo_share does not run at runtime.

The phrasing "directly or by explicit cascade code" is ambiguous. It could mean direct DELETE statements, explicit application-level cascade logic, or schema-defined database cascades. The distinction between these interpretations needs clarification.

Three tables are affected by DeleteMemo. The memo table is deleted directly. The memo_relation and attachment tables are deleted through explicit cascade logic in store/memo.go.

memo_share is only affected by database-level ON DELETE CASCADE. It is not touched by explicit application code in DeleteMemo.

Comment memos are handled recursively. Each comment memo row triggers the same table deletions.

Reaction rows are listed but never deleted. They are unaffected.

Other potential cascade paths such as inbox cleanup are being checked.

-- memo_share stores per-memo share grants (one row per share link).
-- uid is the opaque bearer token included in the share URL.
-- ON DELETE CASCADE ensures grants are cleaned up when the parent memo is deleted.
CREATE TABLE memo_share (
  id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  uid        TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  memo_id    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  creator_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  created_ts BIGINT  NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%s', 'now')),
  expires_ts BIGINT  DEFAULT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY (memo_id) REFERENCES memo(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE INDEX idx_memo_share_memo_id ON memo_share(memo_id);

When `DeleteMemo` runs, these tables are modified as follows:

The API handler in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` first recursively deletes comment memos via `Store.DeleteMemo`, which repeats the same cascade for each comment row in **`memo`**.
